formation.title: Numunu Sookobitu Rises
formation.text:
From the Llano Estacado the paraibos have summoned the bands: Penateka of the honey-eaters, Yamparika of the root-eaters, Quahadi of the antelope, Nokoni who-turn-back, Kotsoteka the buffalo-eaters. The Spanish horse-stock has long since become the foundation of a new economy; the bison herds still cover the southern plains; northern Mexico pays tribute or burns. The question is what shape the Comanche state should take.

Should Numunu Sookobitu remain the great mobile empire of raid-and-tribute, expanding through the war-band and the captive incorporated as kin? Or should the Comanche consolidate as a sovereign nation among nations, with formal borders, written treaties, and the schoolhouse Numic alphabet?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Continental empire: the raid is the state.

modifiers.name: Continental Empire
modifiers.text: Numunu Sookobitu rides as raid-tribute empire. The paraibos and tekwuniwapi command a mobile state extracting tribute from the borderlands, captives absorbed into the nation through the war-band, the bison economy underwriting an empire that moves with the herd.

options.text: Sovereign nation: the council seats permanently.

modifiers.name: Sovereign Nation
modifiers.text: The Comanche nation is consolidated as a state with defined borders, the Council of the Comanche Nation seated permanently, schoolhouse Numic literacy and treaty diplomacy with neighboring powers. The horse empire becomes a nation among nations.

advances.name: Numic Plains Migration
advances.text: The Numunu separate from the broader Shoshonean tradition and migrate south onto the Plains, learning the bison cycle and the seasonal grass.

advances.name: Seasonal Bison Camp
advances.text: Mobile camps follow the bison herds across the Southern Plains, hide-processing at every halt. The foundation of the Plains economy.

advances.name: Numic Skirmisher Tradition
advances.text: Pre-horse Comanche foot-warriors fight in the broken terrain of the canyon country with bow and lance, the older Numic combat style.

advances.name: Puhakat Medicine Bundle
advances.text: Each warrior carries a medicine bundle assembled from his vision quest. The puhakat tradition binds the Comanche to ancestral spirits and confers protection in the raid.

advances.name: Council Lodge Tradition
advances.text: The paraibos of each band gather at the council lodge to debate matters of war and peace, no decision binding without consensus among the bands.

advances.name: Big Dipper Navigation
advances.text: The Comanche navigate by the Big Dipper as cosmological pole and earthly compass, riding by night across the trackless Llano to springs no outsider can find.

advances.name: Comanche Horse Mastery
advances.text: After the Pueblo Revolt of 1680 scatters the Spanish herds, the Comanche become the most accomplished light cavalry on the continent. Every warrior owns horses; the bands move with the herd.

event.title: The Horse Returns to the Plains
event.text:
The Pueblo Revolt of 1680 has scattered the Spanish horse herds across the Southern Plains. What was once a luxury gifted to a few chiefs becomes the everyday property of every Comanche warrior. The Numunu transform from foot-skirmishers into the most accomplished light cavalry the continent has ever seen, the herds following the bison cycle as the warriors follow the herds.

The paraibos must decide how to wield this new mobility: press the raids deep into Mexico while the advantage is fresh, or consolidate the herds and the absorbed warriors into a deeper army?

options.text: Press the raids while the Spanish are stunned!

modifiers.name: Press the Raid
modifiers.text: The seasonal raid-cycle into Texas, Coahuila, and Nuevo Leon strips the northern Mexican provinces of livestock and captives. The horse-warriors return laden.

options.text: Build the herds and fold absorbed warriors into the bands.

modifiers.name: Consolidate the Raid
modifiers.text: Captured horses and the absorbed warriors are folded into the bands. The army grows through the raid rather than being expended in it.

advances.name: Paraibos Confederation
advances.text: The five great bands (Penateka, Yamparika, Quahadi, Nokoni, Kotsoteka) confederate under a paraibos council. The peace chief and tekwuniwapi war chief speak with separate authority.

advances.name: Comanche Horse Warrior
advances.text: The iconic Plains horse-archer, fighting from the saddle with bow and Spanish lance, fluent in maneuvers no European cavalry could match.

advances.name: Pueblo Lessons
advances.text: Captured Pueblo silversmiths, weavers, and horse-grooms teach their crafts to the bands. The first wave of the captive-incorporation engine.

advances.name: Buffalo Hide Trade
advances.text: Bison hides become the bulk export of Comancheria. Hide processing is industrialized at the seasonal camps; the bands trade hides for metal goods at Comanchero outposts.

advances.name: Tekwuniwapi Doctrine
advances.text: The war-chief commands by acclamation, leading raids by personal example. Authority in war is earned in the saddle, not inherited from the council.

advances.name: Comanchero Trade Network
advances.text: New Mexican traders are licensed to cross the Llano and trade with the bands. The borderlands trade circuit makes Santa Fe a Comanche-dependent market.

event.title: The Comanchero Trade
event.text:
The Comancheros (New Mexican traders licensed by the Comanche to cross the Llano) arrive at the encampments with metal goods, weapons, dried chiles. They depart with horses, bison hides, and captives bound for the Santa Fe market. This is the borderlands trade circuit: a parasitic economy on the Spanish frontier, the Comanche its sole sovereign.

Should the council license the Comancheros formally as the Comanche trade arm, extracting a share of every caravan, or should the Comanche send their own riders south, cutting out the New Mexican middleman entirely?

options.text: License the Comancheros: let them work for us.

modifiers.name: Comanchero License
modifiers.text: The New Mexican traders are licensed to enter Comancheria. Caravans cross the Llano carrying weapons and metal goods northward, returning with horses, hides, and captives bound for the Santa Fe market.

options.text: Send Comanche caravans direct to Santa Fe.

modifiers.name: Direct Caravan Trade
modifiers.text: The Comanche send their own caravans south to Santa Fe and east to the Anglo settlements. No middleman takes a share of the borderlands trade.

advances.name: Captive Incorporation
advances.text: Mexican, Pueblo, and Anglo captives are adopted as Comanche children, marry into the bands, and become full Numunu within a generation. The nation grows through absorption.

event.title: The Absorbed Nations
event.text:
A captive Mexican woman, taken at twelve, has borne three Comanche sons and now sits as the senior wife of a Penateka war-chief. A Pueblo silversmith, abducted from Taos in his youth, hammers Comanche bridle ornaments. An Anglo orphan, raised among the Yamparika, speaks no English and counts coup beside his adopted brothers.

This is how the Comanche grew: not as a closed bloodline but as a nation that absorbed its captives into kinship. The council debates whether the nation should formalize this engine of assimilation, or instead extract tribute from the captured: ransoming them back to their kin and turning the raid-cycle into a continental treasury.

options.text: Adopt the captives: the nation grows by absorption.

modifiers.name: The Absorbed Nations
modifiers.text: Mexicans, Pueblos, Anglos taken in raids are adopted, raised as Comanche children, marrying into the bands. The Comanche become a multi-ethnic nation through the captive-incorporation engine.

options.text: Ransom the captives: the raid funds the treasury.

modifiers.name: Tribute Extraction
modifiers.text: Captives are ransomed back to their kin for horses, weapons, and silver. The seasonal raid-cycle becomes a tribute system underwriting the imperial treasury.

advances.name: Raid-Economy
advances.text: The seasonal raid-cycle becomes the central economic activity of the empire. Northern Mexican provinces pay tribute or burn; the Comanche treasury fills with horses and silver.

advances.name: Raider Doctrine
advances.text: A specialized cavalry arm (light, fast, self-supplied for the long ride) is separated from the main horse-warrior tradition for the dedicated raid into Mexico.

advances.name: Horse Aristocracy
advances.text: Wealth in Comancheria is counted in horses. A man with a hundred horses speaks at the council; a man with five hundred gives his daughters in alliance to neighboring bands.

advances.name: Strategic Bison Monopoly
advances.text: The Comanche control the bison herds of the Southern Plains by enforcing seasonal hunting boundaries against rival nations. The herd is the empire's strategic resource.

advances.name: Council of the Comanche Nation
advances.text: The paraibos confederation is formalized as the Council of the Comanche Nation: a permanent senate of band-chiefs that binds the entire confederation to common policy.

advances.name: Llano Estacado Heartland
advances.text: The Staked Plain is fortified as the Comanche refuge: the inviolable Quahadi heartland where no outside army can survive without a Comanche guide.

event.title: The Llano Estacado Heartland
event.text:
The Llano Estacado (the Staked Plain) is the Quahadi heartland and the Comanche refuge. A mesa-top sea of grass three hundred miles across, with no landmark, no surface water the outsider can find. Spanish columns vanished here in the 1700s; American cavalry would later vanish here too. The Quahadi guides navigate by Big Dipper and the memory of generations, leading the bands to hidden springs at predawn.

The council fortifies the heartland: war-camps at every approach, supply caches along the secret paths, the Llano declared the inviolable sanctuary of the Comanche state.

options.text: The Llano is sealed.

modifiers.name: Llano Estacado Refuge
modifiers.text: The Llano Estacado is a sea of grass with no landmark, no water source the outsider knows. To enter is to die of thirst; the Quahadi navigate it by Big Dipper and memory.

advances.name: Imperial Tribute System
advances.text: Northern Mexican provinces pay annual tribute in horses, silver, and trade-license to escape the raid-cycle. The Comanche treasury reaches its peak.

advances.name: Medicine Lodge Tradition
advances.text: Permanent medicine lodges house the puhakat, the medicine men whose bundles bind the bands to ancestral spirits.

advances.name: Horse Breeding Program
advances.text: Selective breeding from the Spanish, Pueblo, and absorbed Anglo bloodlines produces the Comanche pony (small, sturdy, unmatched on the Plains).

advances.name: Great Raid Doctrine
advances.text: The annual late-summer raid into Mexico is regularized as a doctrinal campaign: eight hundred warriors riding south, three months on the trail, returning with the captures of a season.

event.title: The Great Raid
event.text:
Eight hundred Comanche horse-warriors ride south out of the Llano in late summer. Three weeks later the Coahuila haciendas burn for two hundred miles; the captives (children, women, horses by the thousand) return north with the war-band. This is not a campaign but a season. Northern Mexico has paid this tribute for a century.

Does the council press the raid harder, while the Mexican states are absorbed in their civil wars? Or consolidate the gains and rotate the warriors home to teach the new horse-doctrine to a fresh generation?

options.text: Press the raid: Mexico is open.

modifiers.name: Bajio Offensive
modifiers.text: The eight-hundred-warrior column rides past Saltillo and Monterrey into the Bajio itself. Zacatecas burns; the haciendas of San Luis Potosi pay or empty. Every cycle the line of war moves south.

options.text: Rotate the warriors: train the next generation.

modifiers.name: Tributary Frontier
modifiers.text: Northern Mexico is no longer raided so much as taxed. Provincial governors negotiate annual payments in horses, silver, and captives ransomed; the Comancheria treasury runs on Mexican peso.

advances.name: Council Hill Diplomacy
advances.text: The great parliament-stone east of the Wichita range receives embassies from Texas, the United States, and the Mexican governors. The Comanche speak as a continental power.

event.title: Council Hill
event.text:
At Council Hill, the great parliament-stone east of the Wichita range, the paraibos receive emissaries from Texas, from the United States, from the Mexican governors. Each delegation arrives bearing gifts; each departs with a treaty written in a hand the Comanche can now read.

The question before the council is the diplomatic posture itself: should the Comanche speak to neighbors as a continental compact, the senior signatory among the Plains nations? Or should every embassy be received as supplicants beside fortified war-camps, peace negotiated only from a position of armed superiority?

options.text: Continental compact: speak as the senior power.

modifiers.name: Council Hill Compact
modifiers.text: At Council Hill the paraibos negotiate a continental compact, embassies received with formal protocol. The Comanche speak as the senior power of the Southern Plains.

options.text: Armed peace: every embassy beside a war-camp.

modifiers.name: Armed Peace
modifiers.text: Peace from a position of strength: every concession from neighbors is mirrored by a fortified Comanche encampment. The horse herds remain saddled, ready.

advances.name: Strategic Bison Economy
advances.text: The bison herds are managed as the strategic foundation of the empire: hunting quotas, seasonal sanctuaries, the herd defended as state property.

advances.name: Frontier Diplomacy
advances.text: Permanent diplomatic missions in San Antonio, Santa Fe, and Washington negotiate the borderlands as a triangular state-system, the Comanche the senior partner.

advances.name: Eagle Warrior Aristocracy
advances.text: An elite cavalry of the high empire, drawn from the great horse-aristocrat lineages, the Eagle Warriors lead the Great Raid and command at Council Hill.

advances.name: Quahadi Homeland
advances.text: The Quahadi band, the antelope-eaters of the Llano, fortify the heartland with hidden supply caches and the secret water-paths only their guides remember.

advances.name: Borderland Caravan Network
advances.text: Comanche caravans extend north to the Arkansas, south to Saltillo, east to the Red River. The borderlands trade circuit is fully Comanche-administered.

advances.name: Numic Schoolhouse Literacy
advances.text: Numu Tekwapuha is given written form. The Buffalo songs, puhakat traditions, and council histories enter permanent record. Comanche children read in their own tongue.

event.title: The Numic Alphabet
event.text:
A schoolhouse rises at the council ground. The Comanche language (Numu Tekwapuha) is given written form, the elders dictating the Buffalo songs, the puhakat medicine traditions, the council histories into permanent record. Children learn to read in their own tongue before they ride.

The Comanche, once the most mobile nation on the continent, anchor themselves in script. The nation will outlive the bison.

options.text: Numu Tekwapuha is written.

modifiers.name: Numic Orthography
modifiers.text: The Comanche language is given a written form. Schoolhouse alphabets spread the puhakat traditions, the Buffalo songs, the council histories into permanent record.

advances.name: Treaty Diplomacy
advances.text: The Comanche enter the international treaty system as a sovereign signatory, written agreements binding the United States, Mexico, and the Plains nations.

advances.name: Sovereign Endurance
advances.text: Numunu Sookobitu endures past the bison decimation, past the US cavalry, past the dispossession that broke every other Plains nation. The horse empire becomes a permanent state.

advances.name: Modern Plains Cavalry
advances.text: The Comanche horse tradition, modernized with breech-loading carbines and the late-empire saddle. The last buildable Comanche cavalry.

advances.name: Constitution of Comancheria
advances.text: A written constitution formalizes the Council of the Comanche Nation as the legislature of a sovereign state. The horse empire becomes a republic.

advances.name: Industrial Horse Corral
advances.text: Selective breeding programs at scale, modern stables, and a horse-export economy. Comancheria supplies cavalry mounts to half the continent.

destiny.name: Numunu Sookobitu Destiny
destiny.text: The horse empire stands. The paraibos must now decide whether the Numunu state will be ridden as a continental tribute empire or seated as a sovereign nation among nations.

event.title: The Destiny Path Opens
event.text: The paraibos have set the course of the nation. The bands ride forward in the chosen direction: the seasonal raid-cycle deepening into a continental empire, or the council seating itself as the diplomatic core of an Indigenous federation.

options.text: The path is set.

destiny.name: Northern Mexico Tribute Frontier
destiny.text: Take the Tamaulipeco lowlands south of the Rio Grande as the first tribute-frontier of the empire. Own Tamaulipeco and Maratine, taken by the mounted warriors of the bands.

conditions.text: Own Tamaholipa, or a subject owns it
Own Maratine, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Tribute Frontier
event.text: The Comanche horse-warriors have crossed the Rio Grande and broken the Tamaulipeco coast. Maratine pays tribute in livestock and horses; the rancheros of the lower river deliver their seasonal levy to a Comanche embassy. The first true imperial province of Numunu Sookobitu sits south of the river. The horse-empire stretches into Mexico.

options.text: The southern frontier is ours.

destiny.name: Coahuila Dominion
destiny.text: The Guachichil and Coahuila highlands fall to the southern raid. Own Guachichil, Cuencame, and Chisos, make the long raid a doctrine of war, and bring half of the Guachichil country under Comanche rule.

conditions.text: Own Cuauchichil, or a subject owns it
Own Cuencame, or a subject owns it
Own Chisos, or a subject owns it
At least half of the Guachichil area is held by us or our subjects

event.title: Coahuila Falls to the Raid
event.text: Guachichil. Cuencame. Chisos. The high desert of Coahuila and Durango folds under the seasonal raid. Spanish presidios are abandoned; Indigenous communities welcome the Comanche-led collapse of viceregal authority. The question before the council: do the bands press the raid deeper still while the Mexican states reel, or do they fortify what they have taken and absorb the absorbed populations into the empire?

options.text: Press the raid: Mexico is open all the way to Zacatecas!

modifiers.name: Press the Mexican Raid
modifiers.text: While the Mexican states are absorbed in their civil wars, the Comanche raid drives deeper into the highland presidios. Every season the war-band returns laden with captives, horses, and silver.

options.text: Fortify the new dominion: make it permanent.

modifiers.name: Fortify the Borderland
modifiers.text: The conquered Mexican provinces are fortified, hide-camps and horse-corrals built across the new dominion, the absorbed populations integrated into the band system. The empire is made permanent.

destiny.name: Continental Hegemony
destiny.text: Numunu Sookobitu becomes the senior power of the continent. Own Mapimi, Cuanales, Alazapa, and Xumani; set the tribute system over the conquered country; hold 75 prestige and 3000 gold. Unlocks the Imperial Bison-Council Hall.

conditions.text: Own Mapimi, or a subject owns it
Own Cuanales, or a subject owns it
Own Alazapa, or a subject owns it
Own Xumani, or a subject owns it

event.title: Continental Hegemony
event.text: Mapimi, Cuanales, Alazapa, Xumani: from the Bolson de Mapimi to the Sierra Madre, from Nuevo Leon to the Chihuahuan plateau, the continental empire holds. The paraibos sit at the apex of an imperial structure that subordinates every settled state of northern Mexico. The council debates the form of the empire's permanent administration: a viceregal structure modeled on the absorbed Spanish institutions, or a tribute-and-treasury system in the Comanche style?

options.text: Establish a Comanche viceroyalty over the conquests.

modifiers.name: Continental Viceroyalty
modifiers.text: A Comanche viceregal structure replaces the broken Spanish institutions, paraibos seated as imperial governors over the absorbed provinces. The clergy of every faith bow to the council, but Anglo missionaries are turned away from the new empire's reach.

options.text: Convert tribute into a unified continental treasury.

modifiers.name: Unified Continental Treasury
modifiers.text: Tribute from northern Mexico, the Comanchero trade, and the bison hide export are unified under a single imperial treasury. The borderland traders and absorbed merchants are brought into the council; inflation is controlled, credit is cheap, the empire prospers.

destiny.name: Regional Indigenous Alliance
destiny.text: Bring two neighbouring peoples under Comanche protection as subjects, and hold 50 prestige and 25 stability. The first foundations of the sovereign Comanche state are laid in council protocol and in the word given between nations.

event.title: The Council of Allied Nations
event.text: At the council ground the paraibos receive the first formal embassies from the surrounding nations: Apache, Kiowa, Pueblo. The Comanche language has been given written form; treaties are signed in a hand the bands can read. The work of the sovereign Comanche state begins not in the war-camp but in the chamber.

options.text: The Indigenous alliance takes shape.

destiny.name: Plains-Wide Indigenous Coalition
destiny.text: Pivot the Plains nations into a Comanche-led coalition: hold three peoples as subjects. Own He Sapa (the Black Hills) and Awatixa (the Mandan villages); hold 2000 gold and 50 prestige.

conditions.text: Own He Sapa, or a subject owns it
Own Awatixa, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Plains-Wide Coalition
event.text: The Black Hills are sacred to the Lakota; the Missouri river-villages are home to the Mandan and the Hidatsa. The Comanche council has extended its reach to bring these northern nations into the confederation, envoys carrying the Numunu language and the treaty terms up the Plains corridor. The council debates the form of the wider coalition: a council-of-equals seated permanently at Council Hill, or a network of mobile diplomatic envoys reaching every Indigenous capital from the Apache lands to the Great Lakes?

options.text: Convene a permanent Pan-Plains Council.

modifiers.name: Pan-Plains Council
modifiers.text: The permanent council ground hosts envoys from every Plains nation. Mercenary war-bands are obviated by a coalition levy; devastation from the older raid-cycle is repaired in collective effort.

options.text: Send Comanche envoys to every Indigenous capital.

modifiers.name: Mobile Diplomatic Envoys
modifiers.text: Comanche-trained envoys reach every Indigenous capital from the Apache to the Great Lakes, carrying the Numic script and the treaty texts. The coalition rejects mercenary war-bands as a tool of the European powers.

destiny.name: Pan-Indigenous Confederation
destiny.text: The Comanche-led Indigenous federation is recognized as a sovereign signatory among the great powers, no earlier than the age of the Reformation. Own Iisaxpuatahcheeaashe, Marapa, and Minisose; raise a Council Lodge or a Medicine Lodge in eight places of the realm; hold 75 prestige and 25 stability. Unlocks the Treaty Hall.

conditions.text: Own Iisaxpuatahcheeaashe, or a subject owns it
Own Marapa, or a subject owns it
Own Minisose, or a subject owns it
A Council Lodge or a Medicine Lodge stands in at least 8 of our locations

event.title: The Pan-Indigenous Confederation
event.text: The Bighorn range, Marapa, Minisose. The Comanche-led federation reaches from the Llano Estacado to the Saskatchewan, from the Black Hills to the Mandan riverfront. The United States and Mexico negotiate as equals; the United Kingdom sends a chargé d'affaires. The Comanche become the sovereign pivot of an Indigenous bloc in the international system. The council closes the question with a single decision: shall the federation rest on the Pan-Indigenous Pact of council protocol and shared spirituality, or on a written constitution binding every signatory nation as a federal subject?

options.text: Pan-Indigenous Pact: council protocol and the Buffalo song bind us.

modifiers.name: Pan-Indigenous Pact
modifiers.text: The federation rests on council protocol and the shared spirituality of the Plains. The Buffalo song binds the coalition; the puhakat speak with one voice; building the council infrastructure is the duty of every signatory band.

options.text: Constitutional Pact: written federation, every nation a signatory.

modifiers.name: Constitutional Pact
modifiers.text: A written federal constitution binds every Indigenous signatory as a sovereign subject of the Comanche-led confederation. Burgher merchants administer the inter-nation trade; envoys range from the Llano to the Arctic.

units.name: Numic Skirmisher
units.text: Pre-horse Comanche foot-warriors with bow and lance, fighting in the broken terrain of the canyon country.

units.name: Comanche Horse Warrior
units.text: The iconic Plains horse-archer, fighting from the saddle with composite bow and Spanish lance, the most accomplished light cavalry on the continent.

units.name: Comanche Raider
units.text: Specialized raid-warfare cavalry, light and self-supplied for the deep ride into Mexico, the engine of the seasonal raid-cycle.

units.name: Eagle Warrior
units.text: Elite cavalry of the high empire, drawn from the great horse-aristocrat lineages, the Eagle Warriors lead the Great Raid.

units.name: Modern Comanche Cavalry
units.text: Late-empire Comanche horse-warriors armed with breech-loading carbines, the survival-era inheritors of the great Plains tradition.

buildings.name: Bison Camp
buildings.text: Mobile hide-processing camp following the bison herds, the foundation of the Plains economy.

buildings.name: Council Lodge
buildings.text: The paraibos of each band gather here to debate war and peace; no decision binding without consensus.

buildings.name: Horse-Training Corral
buildings.text: Comanche horse-aristocracy breeding ground; selective bloodlines from Spanish, Pueblo, and Anglo stock produce the Comanche pony.

children.text: Horses is produced in the market

buildings.name: Comanchero Trading Post
buildings.text: Comanche-licensed New Mexican traders exchange metal goods for horses, hides, and captives bound for Santa Fe.

buildings.name: Llano Estacado Encampment
buildings.text: Fortified war-camp in the Quahadi heartland, hidden water caches and supply depots known only to Comanche guides.

buildings.name: Medicine Lodge
buildings.text: Permanent puhakat shrine housing the medicine bundles that bind the bands to ancestral spirits.

buildings.name: Constitution Hall
buildings.text: The council hall of the modern sovereign Comanche state, where the Council of the Comanche Nation sits as legislature.

buildings.name: Imperial Bison-Council Hall
buildings.text: The apex Numunu polity, where paraibos and tekwuniwapi co-rule the continental empire. Beneath the Bison-Council standard the absorbed nations are governed as imperial provinces.

buildings.name: Treaty Hall and Numic Schoolhouse
buildings.text: The diplomatic chamber of the sovereign Comanche state, with the Numic schoolhouse adjoined. Treaties with the United States, Mexico, and the Indigenous nations are drafted, debated, signed, and archived under one roof.

list.name: Council of the Comanche Nation
list.text: The inter-band assembly under the dual paraibos and tekwuniwapi co-rulership. The paraibos (peace chiefs) negotiated tribute, captive-ransom, and the Comanchero licenses; the tekwuniwapi (war chiefs) led the raid-cycle. When the divisions converged at Council Hill or Big Spring the paired authority was raised over all five hordes at once, ratifying peace, war, and inter-band redistribution. Maintained, the council speaks with one voice; neglected, the paraibos and tekwuniwapi pull in opposite directions and the federation rides without a line.

list.name: Multi-Horde Federation
list.text: The five-division federal structure binding Penateka of the honey-eaters, Yamparika of the root-eaters, Quahadi of the antelope, Nokoni who-turn-back, and Kotsoteka the buffalo-eaters. Each horde kept its own paraibos and its own raid-radius: Penateka south to Coahuila, Quahadi west across the Llano Estacado, Yamparika north to the Arkansas. The federation pooled the divisions for war and ratified peace at the inter-band council, but never abolished division-level autonomy. Maintained, each horde governs its own territory; neglected, the divisions ride against each other and the council at Council Hill cannot gather a quorum.

list.name: Comanchero Trade License
list.text: The Comanche-administered customs system regulating the Hispanic and Pueblo traders (the comancheros) who entered Comancheria to deal in horses, hides, captives, and silver. The Comanche granted licenses, fixed exchange rates at the rendezvous-fairs, and took a cut of every caravan. By the 1830s the comancheros operated under a recognized customs regime, returning yearly to fixed waterholes the paraibos had designated as licensed marts. Texan accounts describe a non-state with working tariff machinery. Maintained, the marts feed the federation's treasury; neglected, they decay into smuggling routes and the older bands accuse the paraibos of growing rich off Pueblo merchants.

list.name: Captive-Incorporation System
list.text: The institutionalized practice of absorbing captives (Mexican, Pueblo, Anglo) into Comanche bands as adopted kin. Captives were taken in raid, ransomed to their relatives for horses or silver, or, if young, raised as Comanche children and married into the lineages. By the nineteenth century, sizeable percentages of Comanche population were captive-descended Mexican or Anglo, and the institution had become the federation's demographic engine. Maintained, captives become Comanche and the multi-ethnic federation grows; neglected, the unassimilated form a resentful faction and the older lineages complain that the bands have been diluted.
